highlights:
Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU rates for the H100, H200 and B200, read on 3 November 2026, with published commitment discounts and what else changes the bill.

C Compute · H100 list rates, per GPU-hour Rates read 3 November 2026

...

## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

...

Sakura Internet 5% for 6 months, 10% for 12

Each provider's own pages, read 3 Nov 2026. Discounts off list rates.

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.
- Google Cloud lists Flexible Savings Plan rates on the Vertex AI page. For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025. Those are cuts from its earlier prices, not discounts off today's rate.
- Nebius and Lambda name no percentage. Both point large buyers to sales.

highlights:
CoreWeave Cloud Pricing 2026: GPU Rates | ProgramCode

Price check · Nov 6, 2026

# CoreWeave Cloud pricing

Hourly instance pricing spans GPU and CPU workloads; compare on-demand and spot rates, then confirm the full cost with sales.

Edited by Edward Teller· Updated Nov 6, 2026

6.5/10 Value score

Short answer

Paid plans start at $3.27/mo.

CoreWeave Cloud has no listed free plan or free trial. The pricing page lists on-demand and spot compute rates per instance-hour, with prices varying by hardware, region and availability. Spot starts at $3.27 per hour for Intel Emerald Rapids (8562Y+), General Purpose (High Memory); some on-demand rates require contacting sales. Inference GPU rates are listed separately for North America. Budget by workload runtime and confirm storage, networking and other charges with CoreWeave before deployment.

results.title: CoreWeave pricing: every GPU node, Sep 2026
highlights:
On CoreWeave's pricing page, checked 28 September 2026, the HGX B200 is the dearest self-serve GPU node at $68.80 per node-hour ($8.60 per GPU-hour) and the one-GPU GH200 the cheapest at $6.50.

...

The NVIDIA HGX B200 is CoreWeave’s most expensive GPU node with a published on-demand price: $68.80 per node-hour for eight GPUs, or $8.60 per GPU-hour, on CoreWeave’s pricing page checked 28 September 2026. 1 The page lists twelve GPU nodes. Nine carry an on-demand price, and the cheapest is a single GH200 at $6.50 an hour. 1 Per GPU, on-demand runs from $1.25 for an L40 to $10.50 for a GB200 NVL72. Spot prices in North America sit 37% to 60% below on-demand where both are listed. 1

...

Per-GPU-hour figures are Memetik’s arithmetic: node price divided by the page’s GPU Count, rounded half up to the cent. For the GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72, a footnote sets the count at four. Each instance holds two Superchips, and each Superchip has one Grace CPU and two Blackwell GPUs. 1 Ten quotients run past the cent. Their exact values are $6.155 (H100 on-demand) and $6.305 (H200 on-demand). On spot they are $4.26375 (B200), $2.61625 (H200), $2.46375 (H100), $1.38625 (RTX PRO 6000 High Memory), $1.20625 (A100), $1.195 (RTX PRO 6000 Standard Memory), $0.985 (L40S) and $0.78375 (L40). Spot discounts are one minus spot divided by on-demand. CPU-only nodes, storage and networking sit on the same page and are left out of the ranking. How Memetik treats company-published prices is set out in our research methodology.

## What does each CoreWeave GPU node cost per hour?

The HGX B200 heads the ranking at $68.80 per node-hour, and the one-GPU GH200 sits last at $6.50. All figures below come from CoreWeave’s North America table, checked 28 September 2026. 1

...

## What does a CoreWeave GPU cost per GPU-hour?

Memetik reads CoreWeave’s per-GPU-hour rate as a comparison unit. On demand it runs from $1.25 (L40) to $10.50 (GB200 NVL72). Outside CoreWeave’s inference platform, the smallest purchase is a whole node. 1

In ascending order, the on-demand per-GPU rates are L40 $1.25, L40S $2.25 and RTX PRO 6000 High Memory $2.50. A100 follows at $2.70, then H100 $6.16, H200 $6.31, GH200 $6.50, B200 $8.60 and GB200 NVL72 $10.50. 1

CoreWeave prints these figures itself. The North America table carries a column called Inference Single GPU Price (Per Hour). Each of its nine prices matches node price divided by GPU count at the rounding used here. It lists $6.16 for the H100, $6.31 for the H200 and $10.50 for the GB200 NVL72. 1 A footnote limits that column: “Pricing based on GPUs is exclusively applicable to the CoreWeave inference platform customers.” 1 The Europe table has no such column.

The decision changes with utilisation. A team that fills all eight GPUs pays the per-GPU rate. A team that needs two H100s still pays $49.24 an hour for the node, which is $24.62 per working GPU. The lowest self-serve on-demand entry points are the one-GPU GH200 at $6.50 an hour and the eight-GPU L40 node at $10.00. 1 Test the choice against one real workload: the GPU count it keeps busy, its hours per month and the memory it needs per GPU.

results.title: CoreWeave and Nebius shares lost more than two-fifths of their value between October 2 and November 2, 2026. Their price lists did not move: CoreWeave's published H100 SXM read $6.16 and Nebius's … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
CoreWeave and Nebius shares lost more than two-fifths of their value between October 2 and November 2, 2026. Their price lists did not move: CoreWeave's published H100 SXM read $6.16 and Nebius's $4.50 in every weekly catalog we captured, October 4 to November 2.

The market index moved instead. Ornn's Compute Price Index (OCPI), a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, rose for H100 SXM from $2.72 on October 2 to $3.02 on November 1, 2026, and for B200 from $7.88 to $9.44. Across the nine providers we track, the lowest published price in each family ended the month where it started. This week's issue puts that in one table.

Verda raises prices for the tenth time — eight GPUs up about 1%, the L40S holds | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Verda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026, against the figures read there on Nov 5: eight of Verda's nine tracked GPUs rose by about 1% — the tenth rise since Oct 23. The L40S held, the first card Verda has left flat on a rise day in this run. The same morning, Lambda announced rises of about 15% for Nov 16.

...

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 6, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.31 → $13.44 [$13.44], B300 $11.57 → $11.69 [$11.69], B200 $9.05 → $9.14 [$9.138], H200 $6.38 → $6.44 [$6.440], H100 SXM $4.89 → $4.94 [$4.938], A100 80GB $2.29 → $2.32 [$2.316], A100 40GB $1.64 → $1.66 [$1.657] and RTX PRO 6000 $2.70 → $2.73 [$2.725]. The L40S held at $1.94 [$1.939]. Each rise is within a whisker of +1.0% — the same uniform list adjustment as the nine before it.

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $66 per B200 and $36 per H100 on a 730-hour month.

Checked today and unchanged: RunPod Secure, Nebius, CoreWeave, Thunder Compute, TensorDock and SaladCloud all held at the rates read on Nov 5. Not checked today, and named rather than covered by the stamp: Hyperstack (its pricing table could not be read, for the ninth straight day), Lambda's currently-effective rates (now visible only after logging in; its announced Nov 16 rates are reported separately today), RunPod Community (its tier could not be separated in today's read) and nafnaf.ai (its homepage showed no GPUs available today).

results.title: Verda raises prices again — all nine GPUs up about 1%, the eighth rise since Oct 23 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Verda's own pricing page today, Nov 2, 2026, against the figures read there on Nov 1: every GPU in Verda's range rose by about 1% — GB300, B300, B200, H200, H100, both A100s, the RTX PRO 6000 and the L40S. After two flat checks, the October rise run has resumed.

Image: Verda via verda.com

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 2, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.05 → $13.18 [$13.18], B300 $11.35 → $11.46 [$11.46], B200 $8.87 → $8.96 [$8.958], H200 $6.25 → $6.31 [$6.313], H100 SXM $4.79 → $4.84 [$4.841], A100 80GB $2.25 → $2.27 [$2.270], A100 40GB $1.61 → $1.63 [$1.625], RTX PRO 6000 $2.65 → $2.67 [$2.671] and L40S $1.90 → $1.92 [$1.920]. Each move is within a cent of +1.0% — a uniform list adjustment, not one card repricing.

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $65 per B200 and $35 per H100 on a 730-hour month — small per hour, real per fleet.

Checked today and unchanged: RunPod Secure, Lambda, Nebius, CoreWeave, Thunder Compute and TensorDock all held at the rates read on Nov 1, and SaladCloud's new Priority rates (RTX 5090 High $0.60, RTX 4090 High $0.44) are still the live ones. Not checked today, and named rather than covered by the stamp: RunPod Community (its tier could not be separated in today's read), Hyperstack (its pricing table could not be read) and nafnaf.ai (its homepage showed no GPUs available today, so there was no live listing to verify).
